content_html_sanitized:
Posted January 31, 2003
Exclusive to MarijuanaNews
Late last year Vancouver elected a new progressive City Council, virtually all of whom are anti-prohibitionist. This afternoon over half of them visited the New Amsterdam smoke-friendly café on the Hastings Street pot block.

They crowded into and around a booth and drank coffee and surveyed the scene where Steve Tuck smoked hash with in the presence of the DEAland Drug Czar, John Walters.
See
 Steve Tuck Smokes Hash with John Walters As Czar Visits Vancouver's New Amsterdam Cafe. Another One We Couldn't Make Up. Of course, Walters Didn't Smoke with Steve, But.. Special to MarijuanaNews

Walters didn't get it, of course, but they did.

It was before 4:20, so the cannabis (and tobacco) smoking was confined to the glassed-in and ventilated (therefore politically correct) smoking room. In any case, they were there to check out the ambience, not the weed, and they left very favorably impressed.

I am convinced that they understand that places like the New Amsterdam and its sibling, Blunt Bros., are exactly what the city needs, but with a legal source of cannabis. They are also not going to be intimidated by DEAland bluster. Canadians and especially British Columbian are not too pleased with their bullying neighbor to the south right now.
See
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

Canadian cannabis legislation is controlled by the Federal parliament, so there is nothing that the City Council or the BC legislature can do about the laws, but they do have great influence over the police policies. This may be of even greater importance if the Parliament passes a phony decriminalization that authorizes large fines as an incentive for the police to waste more time on cannabis arrests.
See
 Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.

The current policy in Vancouver is not to arrest for possession of anything, but I think that the Council also understands the importance of legalizing cannabis in coping with the city's hideous hard drug scene.
See
 Marijuana Legalization, The Missing Pillar in Solving the Substance Abuse Problem in Vancouver and All of Canada. Analysis By Richard Cowan

After I left the New Amsterdam I walked east on Hastings Street into the heart of darkness. The contrast was surreal. Here in this incredibly beautiful city there are several blocks of grotesque misery.

It is essential to separate the cannabis and hard drug markets, the way that the Dutch have so successfully done, to keep kids and tourists away from the hard drug scene.
See
 Leading Dutch Anti-Prohibitionists Say, The Quality Of The Drugs-Debate Is Abominable.
and links.

But it is also vital that the desperately sick and lonely people who inhabit the hard drug world have access to cannabis to help them with the misery of their lives. Even officially sanctioned medical access to cannabis is too difficult for them. Only when cannabis is as legal and easy to get as alcohol and tobacco will these people be able to get what they need.

I want to see upscale coffee shops, but there has to be a place for these people too. They live in a continuum of pain and despair in which the distinctions between medical and recreational are truly meaningless. This is true of the poor everywhere, and beautiful Vancouver is no exception.
See
 World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan
